subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Cost of Disruption
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Cost of Disruption.

hook.text: A major supply chain disruption costs the average company 6–10% of annual revenue. Some never recover.

buildup.text: Disruptions cause lost sales, expediting costs, customer defection, and stock price drops.

discovery.text: Research shows companies hit by disruptions see stock prices fall 33–40% over two years on average.

twist.text: The indirect costs—brand damage, lost customers, regulatory fines—often exceed the direct operational loss.

climax.text: Every dollar spent on prevention saves 5–10 dollars in disruption costs. Risk management pays for itself.

punchline.text: Disruption costs are measured in revenue, reputation, and years.

quiz.question: How do major disruptions affect stock prices?
